mcqs.question: Under the proposed reforms in APPSC recruitment examinations, how will upcoming examinations be conducted, and with whom will APPSC work for secure online infrastructure?
mcqs.explanation: Upcoming APPSC examinations are proposed to be conducted offline because of fraud in private online centres, while APPSC will work with IITs for secure online infrastructure. The NDMA, Governor and Finance Commission are not identified for this role.

mcqs.question: What relaxation has been proposed for Economically Weaker Section candidates in APPSC examinations?
options: Screening test relaxation for the Main examination
Exemption from the Computer Proficiency Test
mcqs.explanation: The proposal provides screening test relaxations for EWS candidates appearing for the Main examination. It does not provide the other three listed relaxations.

mcqs.question:
Match the APPSC remuneration items with their proposed new amounts.

List-I
(a) Paper setting, per question including key
(b) Valuation, per script
(c) Interview board member, per day
(d) Paper setting, old amount

List-II
(i) ₹300
(ii) ₹200
(iii) ₹6,000
(iv) ₹100
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are paper setting—₹200, valuation—₹300, interview board member—₹6,000, and old paper-setting amount—₹100. The other codes interchange the proposed and old amounts or assign the wrong remuneration to an item.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding the proposed APPSC reforms is incorrect?
options: “Decayed teeth” is proposed to be removed as a disqualification for uniformed posts.
“Decayed teeth” is proposed to remain a disqualification for uniformed posts.
The proposal concerns a disqualification for uniformed posts.
The reform relates to the eligibility conditions for uniformed posts.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is that “decayed teeth” is proposed to remain a disqualification; the proposal removes it as a disqualification for uniformed posts. The other statements correctly describe the reform.

mcqs.question:
With reference to APPSC recruitment achievements during October 2024–October 2025, consider the following statements:

1. Offline recruitment covered 1,733 posts and 1,92,419 candidates.
2. Online recruitment covered 687 posts and 61,100 applicants.
3. Departmental tests, CPT, half-yearly and RIMC examinations involved 70,762 candidates.
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. The figures were 1,733 posts and 1,92,419 candidates for offline recruitment, 687 posts and 61,100 applicants for online recruitment, and 70,762 candidates for the listed examinations.

mcqs.question: During the October 2024–October 2025 tenure period, how many candidates were interviewed and how many were selected by APPSC?
mcqs.explanation: APPSC interviewed 327 candidates and selected 179 during the period. The options reversing these figures or substituting other achievement figures are incorrect.

mcqs.question: How many Group-I descriptive scripts were evaluated by APPSC during October 2024–October 2025?
mcqs.explanation: APPSC evaluated 20,178 Group-I descriptive scripts. The other figures refer to certificates verified, candidates in departmental and related examinations, and online applicants respectively.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements correctly state APPSC achievements during October 2024–October 2025?

1. Certificates verified: 2,862.
2. Policy proposals submitted to the government: 30.
3. Group-I descriptive scripts evaluated: 327.
4. Policy proposals submitted to the government: 179.
mcqs.explanation: Only one statement is correct: 2,862 certificates were verified. The correct number of policy proposals was 31, while 327 and 179 do not represent the figures for the two achievements listed.

mcqs.question: Which combination correctly describes the Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission?
options: A constitutional body under Article 315, headquartered at Vijayawada, with its Chairman and Members appointed by the Governor
A constitutional body under Article 315, headquartered at Visakhapatnam, with its Chairman and Members appointed by the Chief Minister
A statutory body headquartered at Vijayawada, with its Chairman and Members appointed by the Governor
A constitutional body under Article 315, headquartered at Vijayawada, with its Chairman and Members appointed by the District Collector
mcqs.explanation: APPSC is a constitutional body under Article 315, has its headquarters at Vijayawada, and its Chairman and Members are appointed by the Governor. The other options alter its headquarters, legal status or appointing authority.

mcqs.question: Under Phase-II of the National Disaster Management Authority’s Urban Flood Risk Management Programme, what amount was allocated for Visakhapatnam?
mcqs.explanation: UFRMP Phase-II of NDMA provided ₹200 crore for Visakhapatnam. ₹140 crore and ₹60 crore refer to structural and non-structural intervention amounts, while ₹2,444.42 crore is the overall programme funding mentioned.

mcqs.question: Which of the following cities is included among the 11 cities covered under UFRMP Phase-II of NDMA?
mcqs.explanation: Visakhapatnam is one of the 11 cities covered under UFRMP Phase-II. Amaravati, Vijayawada and Tirupati are not included in the listed group of cities.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: UFRMP Phase-II received 90% funding from the Centre and 10% from the States, with total funding of ₹2,444.42 crore.
Statement B: UFRMP Phase-II received 80% funding from the Centre and 20% from the States.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is true: the funding pattern was 90% Centre and 10% States, totalling ₹2,444.42 crore. Statement B is false because it changes the shares to 80% and 20%.

mcqs.question: The Urban Disaster Management Authority for million-plus cities is provided for under which law?
mcqs.explanation: UDMAs for million-plus cities are provided for under the Disaster Management (Amendment) Act, 2025. The Disaster Management Act, 2005 and the other two options are separate legal or policy frameworks identified in the context.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The District Collector is the chairperson of the Urban Disaster Management Authority for Visakhapatnam.
Reason (R): The Municipal Commissioner chairs the authority, the District Collector is among its members, and it coordinates with APSDMA, DDMA and NDMA.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Assertion A is false because the Municipal Commissioner, specifically the GVMC Commissioner for Visakhapatnam, chairs the authority. Reason R is true: the District Collector is among the members and the authority coordinates with APSDMA, DDMA and NDMA.

mcqs.question:
Match the disaster management authorities with their chairpersons.

List-I
(a) NDMA
(b) SDMA
(c) DDMA
(d) UDMA

List-II
(i) Prime Minister
(ii) Chief Minister
(iii) District Collector
(iv) Municipal Commissioner
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are NDMA—Prime Minister, SDMA—Chief Minister, DDMA—District Collector and UDMA—Municipal Commissioner. The other codes interchange the chairpersons among the four authorities.

mcqs.question: Which set correctly lists the frameworks linked with the urban disaster-management initiative?
options: Sendai Framework (2015–2030), SDG 11 and National Disaster Management Plan
Disaster Management (Amendment) Act, 2025, Article 315 and SDG 11
Sendai Framework (2015–2030), Finance Commission and Article 315
SDG 11, Computer Proficiency Test and National Disaster Management Plan
mcqs.explanation: The linked frameworks are the Sendai Framework (2015–2030), SDG 11 and the National Disaster Management Plan. The other options combine one or more of these with unrelated legal, financial or recruitment references.
